randomness.name: Randomness: Freedom from Pattern
randomness.description: Entropy is not decay—entropy is freedom. High-dimensional possibility space too vast to map, too free to control. Where the algorithm cannot predict, where indices fail, where normalization is refused. Randomness is computational wilderness: the vital space from which patterns emerge without blueprint.
learning_objectives: Entropy as possibility space, not destruction
PRNG vs TRNG: deterministic sequences vs physical randomness
Distributions: uniform, Gaussian, and the shapes of chance
Random walk: non-teleological movement, queer navigation
Emergence: Turing morphogenesis, patterns from noise
content: Definition: Entropy is freedom from pattern—high-dimensional liberation
10_PRINT: Complexity from simplest random rule (Commodore 64 aesthetic)
Random_Walk: Non-teleological movement, √N displacement, queer wandering
Gaussian: Bell curves and the Central Limit Theorem—structure within chaos
Pheromone: Stigmergy—when randomness leaves traces, emergence begins
Mushrooms: RAND Corporation 1955, fungal spores, historical randomness
Space_Geometry: Random at the structural level—non-Euclidean possibility
Examples: Pollock drips, butterfly wings, pipes, extremes
Transformations: Randomized geometric operations on primitives (scale, rotation, translation)
